hint.label: Vocabulary

atoms.b: With the exception of the Appalachian Mountains, the Eastern United States are rather flat. The ((++West South coast)), however, is extremely mountainous. Mountain ranges, plateaus and valleys stretch along the entire area. The Rocky Mountains form the largest ((++mountain_range ocean city)) in the US, reaching an average elevation of 14,440 ft (4,400 m).

Between the Appalachian and Rocky Mountains lies a vast area of flat grassland known as the Interior Plains. The westernmost part of the Interior Plains is called the Great Plains. They lie directly to the East of the ((++Rocky Atlantic Pacific)) Mountains. The Great Plains are elevated higher than the rest of the ((++Interior Inner Central)) Plains and have a more arid climate.

atoms.text: North America lies between the Pacific Ocean in the West, and the Atlantic Ocean in the East. The biggest inland waters are the Great Lakes, which are situated in the Northern Midwest, bordering on Canada.

instruction.text: Of course there are rivers too! Several states are named after the largest rivers. Choose all states.

atoms.text: The Missouri River originates in the Northwest, flowing Southeast until it joins the Mississippi River.
The Mississippi River stretches from the North of the United States all the way to the South, where it flows into the Atlantic Ocean.
The Colorado River begins in the central West, flowing further to the Southwest until it reaches the coast.
